title: I Enforced the Vinyl-Cutter Queue on the Mentor Who Hijacked My Roll

parts.text: I loaded roll red at 6:07 p.m. and mentor Kit had already sent a job on my unpaid-looking leftover session. The calendar said: BOOK THE CUTTER. FORTY MINUTES. UNLOAD YOUR ROLL. I was twenty-five, member, holding a calendar hold. Kit did not stop. "Mentors are the blade." I photographed the calendar, the hold, and his job on my roll. Then I logged an overlap. At 6:14 the studio manager asked why Kit's job was on my hold. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio manager can see Kit's job on roll red during my cutter hold.

social.video_title: The mentor sent a job on my booked roll — Part 1/2
social.description: Vinyl cutter, a calendar hold, a mentor still cutting. I logged the overlap. Would you have knocked?

parts.text: Kit called it a test cut until the manager asked for the log. I printed the overlap, the photo, and the hold. He unloaded. Kit booked his own forty and told members tests were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when blades exist. Queue now has a second line: MENTORS UNLOAD THE ROLL. I keep my forty. Kit schedules. The cutter finally sounds like a hold, not leftover vinyl. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Overlap log, unloaded roll, and a second line. Was a test ever my hold?
